affectedPublicSurfaces: THE BATCH SHIP TOOL — the single most consequential surface in this epic, because after this slice a Process Order run CAN EXECUTE ITS ONE WRITE. `batch_ship_packages` is registered as a WRITE, CONFIRM agent tool on #1704's domain-registered dispatcher. The client method already exists and is guarded — `integrations/tiktok/resources/fulfillment.py:41` (`def batch_ship_packages(self, *, body: dict[str, Any]) -> dict:`), allowlisted at `integrations/tiktok/capabilities.py:134` (`("POST", re.compile(r"^/fulfillment/\d+/packages/ship$"))`; note the issue body's `capabilities.py:134-135` is a single line 134, and `:135` is the unrelated orders-split regex, and the file is under `integrations/tiktok/`, not `services/execution/`). It has ZERO PRODUCTION CALL SITES; its only caller today is `tests/unit/test_layer2_sandbox_write_contract.py:294`. Ship Package moves the order to `AWAITING_COLLECTION`, generates the label, assigns the carrier and schedules the handover — after it, the buyer can no longer cancel without seller approval. It is irreversible from Juli's side.

THE DOCUMENTS TOOLS — `get_package` and `get_shipping_documents`, both READ. Get Package Detail and Get Package Shipping Document exist ONLY as guard regexes today (`integrations/tiktok/capabilities.py:163-164`, exact) with NO client methods anywhere in `integrations/tiktok/`, so both need real methods built over #1720's captured shapes. DOCUMENTS ARE FETCHED ONLY AFTER THE SHIP CALL AND NEVER BEFORE: the label exists only once shipping has been arranged, and a run that shipped nothing fetches none.

A DELIBERATE CONTRACT REVERSAL, in the same commit. `tests/unit/test_agent_tool_registry_contract.py` pins `fulfillment.process_order` in `EXPECTED_UNREGISTERED_LEGACY_TOOL_NAMES` (`:99-106`) and asserts it at `:201` inside `TestFourKnownUnregisteredLegacyTools` — the issue body's `:98-111` names the constant, not the assertion. Note the namespace: that test governs the LEGACY Celery registry (`services/execution/runner.py`, `is_tool_registered`), where `"process_order_5" -> "fulfillment.process_order"` (`services/execution/tool_routing.py:23`) still has no handler; the AGENT registry is a different object (`services/agent/tools/registry.py`, today holding only the seven product tools in `tools/product.py` and `tools/product_write.py`, with no `tools/fulfillment.py` at all). Register the AGENT tool and update the legacy expectation in ONE change so the two contracts never disagree — and do not conflate them.

THE RE-VERIFY STEP AND THE SUBSET RULE (PO-FR-5, S-FR-5, ADR-092 d.2). A confirmation can sit for FOUR HOURS. Before the write, EVERY confirmed order AND ITS PACKAGES are re-read, the clean predicate is applied a SECOND time, and the executed set is a SUBSET of the confirmed set, NEVER a superset. TikTok may itself have split the order after an address update, which is why the packages are re-read and not just the order. Every order dropped at re-verify is named with its reason for the digest; the params hash still binds the confirmed list.

PER-PACKAGE OUTCOME READING. Batch Ship returns a TOP-LEVEL `code: 0` WITH A PER-PACKAGE `data.errors[]`. A caller that reads the top-level code alone reports PHANTOM SUCCESSES at volume — it tells the seller parcels are on their way that were never arranged. Each per-package error names its order; the failed order is reported failed and the others shipped. The top-level code alone never decides the outcome.

NO route shape changes and no new HTTP endpoint. Under S-NFR-3 the write stays SANDBOX-ONLY until the production-write gate #1339 passes; the sandbox order read path arrives with #1719 and the Batch Ship partial-error shape with #1720.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE IN THIS SLICE. The confirmed list lives in `proposed_change` (existing uncapped JSONB), the tool call is a ledger row on the existing `ToolExecution` model through `services/agent/runner/ledger.py`, and the dropped-order reasons are carried into #1805's completion act rather than persisted here. Do not open a migration file and do not open `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`; migration numbers are RESERVED BY META and never read from head, but the correct action here is not to reserve one — it is to not need one. Stable and candidate run the same schema, so a code rollback needs no downgrade. The new stop reasons (`shipped_all`, `shipped_subset`, `vendor_partial_failure` and the rest) are #1805's migration, NOT this slice's: a run here ends on the EXISTING vocabulary, and a run that fails outright stays on the existing terminal failure path. If implementation concludes a column is needed, that is a signal the slice boundary is wrong — stop and report.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. `batch_ship_packages` keeps its zero production call sites, no agent tool is registered, `fulfillment.process_order` stays pinned as an unregistered legacy tool, and a Process Order run has nothing to execute. No package is arranged, no label is generated, and no seller state changes — the pre-existing state is safe by construction. A partially-correct re-verify must NEVER be merged to unblock #1805 or #1806: the failure mode is a real parcel shipped over a pending cancellation, and that is not recoverable by a redeploy.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: DEREGISTER THE TOOL FIRST — with `batch_ship_packages` off the agent registry, no run can dispatch a ship call, which stops any further write immediately without touching the schema; deregistering also returns `tests/unit/test_agent_tool_registry_contract.py` to its current expectation. Then redeploy the previous release and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker. NO DOWNGRADE IS NEEDED — there is no migration. THE CRITICAL PROPERTY: A PACKAGE ALREADY SHIPPED CANNOT BE UN-SHIPPED BY ANY ROLLBACK. Ship Package generates the label, assigns the carrier and moves the order to `AWAITING_COLLECTION`; after it the buyer cannot cancel without seller approval, and Juli must NEVER attempt a compensating cancel — no cancel tool exists and none may be added. The correct remediation for a wrongly shipped parcel is human: the seller pulls it from the courier pile, and the run's completion act names the order with a deep link. A run paused mid-execution is left to its ledger, which replays a `succeeded` write byte-identically rather than re-issuing it. Because writes are sandbox-only until #1339, the blast radius of a post-cutover failure here is the sandbox shop, not a real seller's orders — that boundary is the whole reason S-NFR-3 exists and it must hold in both directions.

doNotInfer: Do NOT write a migration. The six new stop reasons and their check-constraint change are #1805's slice with its own RESERVED number; a run here ends on the existing vocabulary. Migration numbers are RESERVED BY META and never read from head.

Do NOT build a vendor-refusal branch, and do NOT let any code path assume the platform will block a ship over a pending cancellation. ADR-092's 2026-09-05 amendment: TikTok does NOT refuse — the write goes through and the cancellation is approved anyway. The exclusion is HARD, in Juli's own code, at selection AND again at re-verify. The on-disk ADR Context and `seller-journeys/process-order-actors.md` §E row 3 still say the opposite; they are superseded.

Do NOT decide the outcome from the top-level response code. Batch Ship returns a top-level success WITH per-package `data.errors[]`; reading only the top level reports phantom successes at volume and tells the seller parcels are moving that were never arranged.

Do NOT widen the executed set. It is a SUBSET of the confirmed set, never a superset, however clean an unconfirmed order looks at re-verify. The params hash binds the confirmed list and the seller consented to that list and no other.
Do NOT skip the PACKAGE re-read and re-verify only the order. TikTok may have split the order itself after an address update, so a stale package id is a label for a parcel that no longer exists.
Do NOT cancel anything, ever, and do NOT add a cancel tool. An error string advising cancellation surfaces as a REASON and cancels nothing. Every cancellation is a human act on workflow 8a's surface.

Do NOT add Create Packages or Confirm Package Shipment. In SEA TikTok creates the package at order time (ADR-092 Context defect 1), and Confirm Package Shipment is a certified-warehouse-provider endpoint, not a seller one (defect 2). Neither belongs in Process Order in any version.

Do NOT perform a second write of any kind — no combine, no split, no Ship Package re-arrange, no Update Package Delivery Status, no Mark Package As Shipped (US/EMEA/JP-only, not VN). Exactly one write per run (S-FR-6); the rest are v2.

Do NOT handle FBT or Seller Own Fleet. FBT orders are refused by the vendor anyway (`21008025`) and are monitor-only by design; SOF with `self_shipment` is v2. Both are listed with their reasons and never acted on.
Do NOT choose a handover slot or invent a handover method. The method comes from the shop default; slots are READ, never chosen.
Do NOT fetch documents before the ship call, and do NOT fetch them at all for a run that shipped nothing. The label exists only once shipping has been arranged.

Do NOT bind the tests to a `**kwargs` double. Bind to the REAL `FulfillmentResource.batch_ship_packages` signature (`def batch_ship_packages(self, *, body: dict[str, Any]) -> dict` at `resources/fulfillment.py:41`) and to #1720's CAPTURED response, or the contract break stays invisible.

Do NOT conflate the two registries. `tests/unit/test_agent_tool_registry_contract.py` governs the LEGACY Celery registry (`services/execution/runner.py`, `tool_routing.py:23`); the agent's own `ToolRegistry` lives at `services/agent/tools/registry.py` and holds only the seven product tools today. Update both deliberately in the SAME change so two contracts never disagree.
Do NOT attempt a production write. S-NFR-3 keeps writes sandbox-only until #1339 passes; the production guard must REFUSE by default and that refusal is asserted, not assumed.
Do NOT verify with a success-marker grep. A dispatch that raises before it logs is invisible to one; assert on the ledger row, the outbound request and the run's own state.
Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051); do NOT touch apps/**, packages/** or ios/**, which are on this epic's doNotLoad list.
